questions.stem: Why are archive labels printed instead of handwritten?

options.text: Handwriting fades and is misread during retrieval
Printed labels are cheaper to make
Printers add the review date automatically
Handwritten labels cannot show box numbers

explanations.a: That is the reason the handbook gives.
explanations.c: The review date is not printed on the label.
explanations.d: Any label can show a box number.

questions.stem: A label is damaged and unreadable. What do staff do with the box?

options.text: Replace the label the same day or move the box to intake
Destroy the box after logging it
Leave it until the next review date

explanations.a: Damaged labels are replaced the same day; unreadable boxes wait on intake.
explanations.b: Destruction needs a retention decision, not a damaged label.
explanations.c: Waiting would leave the box unfindable.
explanations.d: The category does not change because of damage.

questions.stem: What happens to a box whose label has no retention category?

options.text: It is never reviewed and its shelf space is wasted
It is treated as permanent and reviewed yearly
It is destroyed after two years by default
It is moved to another collection

explanations.a: Without a category the box never enters review.
explanations.b: There is no default to permanent.
explanations.d: Collections do not change because of a missing category.
